findings.claim: A leftover part is identified only by its current title or a title in memory_versions, which keeps only the newest MaxVersions=5 snapshots. A part renamed and then edited more than 5 times loses its '(part i/N)' title, and a shorter re-save leaves it active. Before this commit the derived-key fallback archived it whatever its title said.

The history match '% (part i/%)' has any total and no document title prefix. An unrelated memory that took a part's key and whose current or past title ends in '(part i/...)' (for example edited to 'Notes (part 2/3)') would be archived. The key is already scoped to this document, so exposure is low.

evidence: Read the diff and internal/memory/save.go (Save, write, update, restore) and ops.go Update. No tests run.
Unrelated holder of the derived key with no matching title or versions stays active; matches TestResavingASplitDocumentSparesAMemoryThatTookAnArchivedPartsKey.
Moved part renamed via mem_update: Update snapshots the old title, so the '~n' branch plus the version-title match archives it; the holder stays active.
Renamed non-moved part: archived through the version-title match.
Unrelated holder of the derived key while the part sits at '~n': stays active; the part is archived.
The '~n' suffix is checked as digits only; the key is not interpolated into LIKE.
Risk: 1 is correct: it changes which existing rows get status='archived'.
